//go:build postingedgebench && darwin

package postingedge

import (
	"github.com/weaviate/weaviate/adapters/repos/db/lsmkv"
)

// What the harness of the diagnostic of the inserts asks of the diagnostic
// branch (bench_diag_test.go): the clocks of the callers, the counts of the
// work of every plan, and the counters of the reads of the store. Its twin
// for m2 as it is does nothing.

// diagBranch tells that this is the diagnostic branch.
const diagBranch = true

// diagHooks turns on what was asked for, in the config of an index that is
// about to open. It returns what reads the clocks of the callers, nil
// without them, and what turns the counters of the store off again.
func diagHooks(cfg *PersistentConfig, clocksOn, work bool) (func() map[string]int64, func()) {
	cfg.planWork = work
	if !clocksOn {
		return nil, func() {}
	}
	clocks := &insertClocks{}
	cfg.clocks = clocks
	lsmkv.Diag.On.Store(true)
	return clocks.snapshot, func() { lsmkv.Diag.On.Store(false) }
}

// diagStore is what the reads of the store consulted so far (lsmkv.Diag).
func diagStore() map[string]int64 {
	return map[string]int64{
		"reads": lsmkv.Diag.Reads.Load(), "segmentsHeld": lsmkv.Diag.Held.Load(),
		"segmentsFound": lsmkv.Diag.Found.Load(), "bloomFalse": lsmkv.Diag.BloomFalse.Load(),
	}
}
